title: Cinna Task Protocol — MCP binding
description: The eight tools every Cinna host (Cinna Desktop, cinna-core agent environments) registers on the MCP server named `cinna`. Both hosts load this file and assert their registered tools match it. Engine-visible names are derived by the host: Claude Code `mcp__cinna__<tool>`, Codex `mcp.cinna.<tool>`, OpenCode `cinna_<tool>`. Status words: `category` is what agents read and write (backlog, ready, active, waiting, done); `tasks_report.status` is the executor's statement (in_progress, blocked, done, failed). A host maps `done → completed` and `failed → error` onto its own status column.

aliases.description: Older tool names, for the record. They are NOT registered as tools (that would double every agent's tool list); a host that must keep talking to environments built before this change keeps them in its pre-approval or name-mapping lists only. Never mentioned in the skill or any prompt. Dropped from those lists in the release after this one.

ref.description: A task reference as this host shows it (`t-3f9a2b1c`, `TASK-5`, a folder task's id). Opaque: never built or translated by the agent, always copied from a tool result or the turn context.

category.description: Where a task sits. `done` covers completed, failed and cancelled work.

custom_fields.description: User-named values on the task: text, number, boolean or a flat list of strings. Keys the protocol owns (status, title, priority, id, execution, origin, depth, group, parent, blocked_by) are refused in any letter case. The whole set is replaced on update; `{}` clears it.

oneOf.description: A path relative to the working folder, or an http(s) URL.

tasks_targets.description: Who you can hand work to. Returns one entry per target with the exact `target` string to pass as `tasks_create.assignee`, its name, kind, where it runs, what it supports and its protocol version. Call it before delegating; never guess a target.

structured_report.description: The target files `tasks_report`; false means its result is read from comments and status.

requires_approval.description: A person approves the run before it starts, whatever `execution` says.

tasks_list.description: The tasks that concern you: assigned to you, created by you, or delegated by you. Newest first, at most 50, closed ones left out unless `include_closed`. Not a wait primitive: if nothing changed since your last call in this turn, end your turn.

tasks_get.description: One task in full: goal, description, status and category, priority, assignee, parent, blocked_by, custom fields, the latest comments, the latest report, and where any attached files were placed for you to read.

tasks_create.description: Create work. Without `assignee` it goes into your own queue (Backlog unless `category: ready`). With an `assignee` from `tasks_targets` it is a delegation: `description` is the brief, `id` makes the request idempotent (repeating it returns the same work), and you end your turn afterwards — the result arrives later as a message in this conversation. `parent` must be a task of yours; with an assignee it makes a delegated subtask. Depth is capped at 2 and at most 20 tool-created tasks per conversation.

description.description: Markdown. For a delegation, everything the executor needs; it may not see this conversation.

category.description: `backlog` (default) or `ready`. `draft` is only for a delegation to a folder target: the brief is written but not picked up until made ready.

assignee.description: A `target` from `tasks_targets`, verbatim. Omit for your own queue.

id.description: Delegations only. Your idempotency key for this request; `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<slug>` is the recommended shape.

execution.description: Delegations only. `ask` forces a person to approve the run; otherwise the receiving side's own setting decides.

group.description: Delegations only. Give several requests the same group and you are woken once, when all of them are over.

tasks_update.description: Edit a task's fields, or move it by hand between Backlog, Ready, Done and Cancelled as a person would on the board. Not for saying how your work went — that is `tasks_report`. Refused on a task something else is working on: a running turn, an open question, a queue or a delegation.

category.description: A manual move. A host with status words of its own (a folder's `_board.yaml`) also accepts one of those words here.

tasks_comment.description: Leave a Markdown note on a task — a finding, an intermediate result, a question for a person reading the task page. Shown on the task and copied to the task's home where it has one. Does not change status; use `tasks_report` for that.

ref.description: Defaults to the task this conversation is working on.

files.description: Paths relative to the working folder to attach, where the host supports attachments. A missing file fails the call and posts nothing.

tasks_report.description: Say how your work on a task is going or how it ended. The only way to close work you were given: `done` or `failed` with a one-line summary before you end your turn; `blocked` with a `question` when you cannot continue (audience `requester` wakes the agent that asked, `user` waits for a person); `in_progress` for a progress note. A dispatched or delegated task that ends without a report is left Waiting with “Ended without reporting”. Idempotent: repeating the same report changes nothing.

ref.description: Defaults to the task this conversation is working on.

summary.description: One line. It is what every list shows.

audience.description: Who a `blocked` question is for. Defaults to `requester` when an agent asked for this work, else `user`.

body.description: The full answer or report, Markdown.

tasks_reply.description: Answer a `blocked` question from work you delegated, or send a follow-up to work still under way. The executor receives it in its own conversation with everything it has already read.

result_packet.description: How a delegation's result reaches the requester: a host-authored message in the requesting conversation, never a tool return. One shape on every host.

context_block.description: Data the host prepends to a turn, never persisted, never instructions. The skill explains it; the block only states facts.
lines: Cinna task context (not part of the conversation):
- chain depth: N · open delegations: T (W waiting on the user) · ready tasks: N   [each only while nonzero]
